title: Relay sync pulse and action queue — operator notes
content:
Shift pulse — quick summary:

- Shift owner: Aisha Patel (UTC night shift).
- Coverage window: 2027-03-17 22:00 UTC -> 2027-03-18 06:00 UTC.
- Purpose: capture handoff context, actions taken for the latency surge at 03:10 UTC, and concrete follow-ups for next rotation.

Timeline (concise):
- 02:58 UTC — small jitter in token-generation latency observed on hosted-api (alerting threshold 95p > 250ms). No user-visible errors yet.
- 03:10 UTC — spike to 95p = 1.2s on route /v1/complete, error rate increased from 0.03% -> 0.9% (mostly 502s from inference proxy).
- 03:12 UTC — on-call pinged via #ops-bridge; started triage.
- 03:14 UTC — confirmed fallback churn: router had rolled traffic to a quantized model variant (q8) due to capacity constraints; KV-cache miss rate jumped, causing repeated cold starts and queueing.
- 03:18 UTC — mitigation A: temporarily increased dedicated pool replica count for hosted-api-route via infra-autoscale (kubectl scale deployment hosted-api-pool --replicas=6) — immediate partial improvement.
- 03:26 UTC — mitigation B: forced router to pin model-variant to prev stable until KV-cache warmed (router-admin toggle: variant.lock=true for route /v1/complete).
- 03:35 UTC — metric stabilization observed; 95p returned to ~300ms, error rate fell to baseline over ~10 mins.
- 04:00 UTC — followup: enacted longer prefix-caching TTL for the route (config: cache.prefix_ttl from 30s -> 300s) as a temporary resilience knob.

Immediate decisions and why:
- Scaling replica count gave headroom quickly; the priority was to reduce request queueing while we investigated the root cause.
- Pinning model variant prevented repeated fallback transitions that were thrashing the cache.
- Longer prefix TTL is a conservative mitigation to reduce repeated KV churn while we scope a proper router change.

Commands and observability checks used (copy/paste friendly):
- Prometheus query (95th latency for route):
  - sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/complete"}[5m])) by (le) -> used histograms to get p95
- Error rate: increase(query): sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/complete",status=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/complete"}[1m]))
- k8s scale: kubectl -n infra scale deployment hosted-api-pool --replicas=6
- Router toggle: curl -X POST $ROUTER_ADMIN/api/routes/pin -d '{"route":"/v1/complete","variant":"stable-v2"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
- Cache TTL change (via config service): curl -X PATCH $CONFIG_API/routes/complete -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"cache":{"prefix_ttl":300}}'
- Logs: gzcat inference-proxy.stderr.log | jq -r '.message' | grep 'fallback' | tail -n 200

Root cause (initial diagnosis):
- Primary contributor: variant fallback churn caused by transient capacity pressure -> resulted in high KV-cache miss rates and repeated cold starts for model KV state.
- Secondary: router lacked a short-term damping policy for variant transitions on high-miss signals; immediate mitigations were tactical (scale + pin + longer TTL).

Runbook draft snippet (to be integrated into KV-Cache and Router playbooks):
1) Detection: alert when (route 95p > 500ms && error_rate > 0.3%) for 2 consecutive 1m windows.
2) Quick diagnostics: check router decision logs, recent variant flips (router-admin /metrics/decisions), and KV-cache miss rate (kv_cache.miss_rate{route}).
3) Immediate actions (order matters):
   a) If queueing detected, scale the dedicated pool by +50% (kubectl scale).
   b) Temporarily pin route to last-known-stable variant for 10m.
   c) Increase prefix_ttl to 300s for the route.
   d) If errors persist >10m, route small percentage (5-10%) to fallback `cheat-mode` (stateless stub) to preserve availability and buy time for fix.
4) Post-incident: collect heap/profile dump from model hosts (s3 artifact), capture sample traces (trace_id list), and create follow-up ticket.

Action items (concrete) — owner and ETA where possible:
- SRE: create JIRA SRE-4821 to implement router damping for variant transitions (Owner: Marco; ETA: 2027-03-24).
- Infra: add an infra-autoscale safety buffer for low-traffic hours to reduce fallback frequency (Owner: Lina; ETA: 2027-03-21).
- Platform: add a route-specific cache warmup policy in router (Owner: model-onboarding team / Priya; ETA: 2027-03-30).
- Observability: add a dedicated p95 by-variant dashboard and an alert that triggers on rapid variant flips within 5m (Owner: Observability; ETA: 2027-03-20).
- Documentation: fold this runbook snippet into Confluence page KV-Cache-Runbook and mark the new detection thresholds (Owner: Aisha; ETA: 2027-03-19).

Notes to next shift (what to watch):
- Watch delta between kv_cache.miss_rate and router.variant_flip_count; set an ad-hoc chart showing both.
- Check infra-autoscale events around 02:00-04:00 UTC for repeated small spikes.
- Confirm that the admin pin remains set; if not, don't un-pin without consulting platform lead.

Outstanding questions / unclear facts:
- Why did autoscaler decide to downsize before the traffic spike? Need controller logs (k-scaler) for 02:30-03:05 UTC.
- Was there any concurrent model deployment in staging that might have leaked capacity signals?
- Are there any long-tail requests that never hit cache due to unusual prompt shapes? (sampling requested).

Post-shift followups I will start:
- Upload collected traces and a 5-min trace window to S3:/sre/incidents/2027-03-17/trace_bundle.tar.gz.
- Create sample prompt set where cache miss rate is high and hand to model-onboarding for analysis.

Slack + comms:
- Posted short incident note to #ops-bridge with TL;DR and link to trace bundle.
- Drafted a customer-facing blurb for incidents channel if needed — kept on hold (marketing/SRE escalation policy).

Misc quick logs/snippets (copied from bridge at 03:16 UTC):
- "router: flip route=/v1/complete from stable-v2 -> q8 at t=03:10:11, reason=capacity_shortage"
- "kv_cache: miss_rate=0.87 window=60s route=/v1/complete"
- "inference-proxy: queued_requests=124 avg_queue_latency=420ms"

Handoff checklist (for incoming):
- Acknowledge this note in the bridge thread.
- Verify all mitigation toggles are still active (scale pinned, TTL=300).
- If new alerts trigger, start with runbook steps 2->3 immediately.
- If unresolved after 30m, escalate to Platform lead (Priya) and trigger a postmortem run.

Signed-off: Aisha Patel
bridge: #ops-bridge | incident-thread: FFb3c9 | artifacts: S3://sre/incidents/2027-03-17/

End of relay sync pulse.
